newsitem.title: USA: U.S. insurers may see drop in auto profits in 1997.
newsitem.headline: U.S. insurers may see drop in auto profits in 1997.

text.p: The U.S. property-casualty insurance industry may see a decline in the profitability of personal automobile insurance in 1997, an industry economist said.

In personal insurance lines segment, "there have been increasing reports of rate decreases in auto insurance," said Sean Mooney, senior vice president and economist at the Insurance Information Institute.
"We may expect to see a decline in profitability in 1997," he said in a statement accompanying a report on the industry's 1996 financial results.
In commercial lines, he said, price competition is expected to continue in 1997.

"There is no sense in the marketplace that prices have reached an unacceptably low level," he said, "While the rate of price decreases could be characterized as mild, there are no clear signs of a return to more adequate rates."
The industry's outlook also will depend on external forces, such as the stock market's performance and catastrophes.
A decline in equity prices along with an increase in interest rates would "severely reduce the industry's ability to record further advances in capital gains," he said.
And as the hurricane season approaches, the insurers and reinsurers "can only keep their fingers crossed that 1997 will not be the year of the Big One."
